title: A bundle includes unused tickets
hook: Five-ticket bundles can force a second bundle for the sixth trip.

knows: that a model can declare hypothetical quantities
doesNotKnow: Compare exact-demand tickets with indivisible ticket bundles.

misconception: A discounted bundle is cheaper for every required trip count.
objective: Compare exact-demand tickets with indivisible ticket bundles.

claims.text: Fictional singles cost €2. A five-ticket bundle costs €8 and cannot be split; leftover tickets are unused here. Scaled model; fictional fares; leftover value=0; no recommendation.
claims.source: Declared hypothetical inputs and limits in resource-specs.json. No actual product, price, tariff, shelf-life, treatment or physical appliance specification is asserted.

claims.text: The stage's two results are computed by the printed expressions. At Trips=6, A=€12 and B=€16. Geometry follows the declared dimension relationships. Other pictures use a fixed full scale across the slider range; continuous fills and arcs show relative amounts rather than literal object counts.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["*",2,"x"]; B=["*",8,["ceil",["/","x",5]]]; x denotes Trips. At x=6, A=12, B=16; recall at x=9: B=16. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. Diagram scale: resourceGraphicScale in resource-model.ts takes the maximum modeled magnitude across both formulas and the declared slider range. For non-geometry figures, full-scale values are displayed; the scale stays fixed when the slider changes. Energy axis endpoints use resourceAxisEnd, including B=5×A hours in lh-watts-hours-trade; cylinder rx and ry both scale with radius in resourceCylinderDimensions.

claims.text: A sixth required trip needs a second complete bundle under this rule. The checkout pays for unused tickets too. Effective use count and purchased count are different denominators.
